name: Gobi Manchurian

ingredients.name: Cauliflower (gobi) florets
ingredients.householdMeasure: 8 to 10 small florets (about ¼ medium head)

ingredients.name: Cornflour (cornstarch)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 tbsp + ½ tsp for batter; 1 tsp for slurry

ingredients.name: Sunflower oil (or other neutral oil), for frying
Green chilli
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ small chilli, slit and chopped

equipment: Small kadai or deep frying pan for frying, with a slotted spoon (no kadai? a deep, heavy saucepan works; the oil should be at least 4 cm deep)
Second pan or wok for the sauce (no wok? use a wide non-stick frying pan on the highest heat)
Mixing bowl and spoon or whisk
Measuring spoons (a normal teaspoon and tablespoon are fine)
Kitchen paper or a plate lined with a clean cloth, to drain the florets
Pot for blanching (optional; or a microwave-safe bowl)
Air fryer or oven (optional, for the Low-oil variant; no air fryer? use an oven at 220 °C or a shallow pan with 2 tbsp oil, turning the florets)

steps.title: Cut the cauliflower
steps.text: Cut 150 g cauliflower into small, even florets, about 3 to 4 cm each.
steps.tip: Equal sizes cook at the same speed.
steps.visualCue: Equal-sized florets, no thick stalks left on
steps.cameraCheck: The cut florets on the board
steps.videoShot: Knife cutting florets off the stalk.

steps.title: Wash and blanch
steps.text: Boil 500 ml water with a pinch of salt; add the florets for 2 minutes. (Optional: the sources say blanching can be skipped if the florets are clean; it also drives out any insects.)
steps.visualCue: Florets turn slightly brighter and tender-crisp, not soft

steps.title: Drain and dry
steps.text: Drain, then spread the florets on a clean cloth or kitchen paper and pat fully dry.
steps.tip: Wet florets make the batter slide off and the oil spit.
steps.visualCue: No water drops on the surface
steps.cameraCheck: The dry florets on the cloth

steps.title: Mix the dry batter
steps.text: In a bowl, mix 15 g (1 tbsp) maida, 12 g (1 tbsp + ½ tsp) cornflour, 0.5 g (¼ tsp) Kashmiri chilli powder, 0.3 g (a pinch) pepper and 1.0 g (a scant ¼ tsp) salt.
steps.cameraCheck: The dry mix in the bowl
steps.videoShot: A spoon stirring the dry mix.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: Add about 30 ml (2 tbsp) water, a little at a time, stirring to a thick, smooth batter.
steps.tip: Too thin and the coating turns patchy; too thick and it is doughy. Add water 1 tsp at a time.
steps.visualCue: Thick and slow-falling, like pancake batter; it should coat the back of a spoon
steps.videoShot: Batter ribbon falling from a spoon.

steps.title: Coat the florets
steps.text: Add the dry florets to the batter and toss until each is lightly coated.
steps.visualCue: Each floret has a thin, even coat, none stuck together in clumps

steps.title: Heat the frying oil
steps.text: Heat about 250 ml oil in the kadai on medium-high.
steps.tip: Oil too cool = greasy florets; too hot = dark outside, raw inside.
steps.visualCue: A drop of batter rises in 3 to 4 seconds with small bubbles
steps.cameraCheck: The batter drop bubbling in the oil
steps.videoShot: A drop of batter sizzling to the surface.

steps.title: Fry in batches
steps.text: Slide in about half the florets one by one; fry on medium-high, turning now and then.
steps.tip: Do not crowd the pan; crowding drops the oil temperature.
steps.visualCue: Pale golden, crisp coat, bubbling slows down
steps.videoShot: Florets turning golden in the kadai.

steps.title: Drain the first batch
steps.text: Lift with a slotted spoon onto kitchen paper.

steps.title: Fry the second batch
steps.text: Repeat step 8 with the rest of the florets.

steps.title: Double-fry for crunch (optional)
steps.text: Put all florets back into the hot oil for 1 minute.
steps.tip: This keeps them crisp longer under the sauce.
steps.visualCue: Deeper golden colour, very crisp when tapped
steps.videoShot: All florets returned to the oil.

steps.title: Prepare the sauce items
steps.text: Finely chop 4 g garlic, 3 g ginger, 2 g green chilli, 20 g spring onion whites; cube 20 g capsicum.
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped aromatics in a small bowl

steps.title: Mix the sauce
steps.text: In a small cup stir 10 ml soy sauce, 15 g ketchup, 5 g red chilli sauce and 2.5 ml vinegar; in another cup mix 4 g (1 tsp) cornflour with 2 tbsp water.
steps.visualCue: Dark red-brown sauce; milky slurry without lumps

steps.title: Heat the sauce pan
steps.text: Heat 5 g (1 tsp) oil in a wok or wide pan on the highest heat.

steps.title: Fry the aromatics
steps.text: Add garlic, ginger and green chilli; stir for 15 seconds.
steps.tip: Burnt garlic turns the sauce bitter, so keep moving it.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add spring onion whites and capsicum; toss on high heat.

steps.title: Add the sauce
steps.text: Pour in the sauce mix and the stirred slurry; stir until it thickens and turns glossy.
steps.tip: For a gravy version, add 100 ml water to the sauce and a second 4 g cornflour slurry; serve straight away.
steps.visualCue: Glossy, thick sauce that clings to the spoon

steps.title: Toss the florets
steps.text: Add the fried florets; toss on high heat for 30 to 40 seconds so they are just coated.
steps.tip: Do not simmer; the coating turns soft in the sauce within minutes.
steps.visualCue: Florets glossy and red-brown, still crisp

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Take off the heat, scatter 5 g (1 tbsp) spring onion greens and serve at once.
steps.visualCue: Glossy red-brown florets with green flecks
steps.videoShot: Florets plated with spring onion sprinkled over.

reasons: cauliflower is a good low-calorie, vitamin C and K base, but the batter and deep-frying add about 17 g of mostly omega-6 oil and about 150 kcal from fat; the sauce brings about 1,150 mg sodium (58% of the daily limit) and some added sugar. Restaurant portions are bigger, fried in reused oil and sauced more heavily.

researchRating.basis: very widely loved as an Indo-Chinese starter; recipe pages carry long comment threads with repeat-cook praise, and every major Indian recipe site has a version; the main complaint is that the coat turns soggy, which careful frying and a quick toss solve.

storage: best eaten fresh. Fridge: up to 1 day in an airtight box (the coat softens; keep the sauce and florets separate if possible). Freezer: not recommended (cauliflower turns watery). Reheat in an air fryer or hot oven at 200 °C for 5 to 6 minutes, or in a dry pan on high heat; avoid the microwave, which makes it soggy.
leftoverRemix: chop leftover florets and stir them through a hot pan of fried rice or noodles with a little extra soy sauce for a Gobi Manchurian fried rice.
burnOff: about 340 kcal ≈ 4.9 km of running (70 kg adult, ~70 kcal per km) or about 7 km of brisk walking (est.).

navratri.reason: maida, soy sauce, garlic, spring onion and ordinary table salt (most common vrat rules assumed)

ekadashi.reason: grain flours (maida, cornflour), garlic and soy sauce (grains and onion-garlic avoided on Ekadashi in the common rule set)

jain.reason: drop garlic, fresh ginger and spring onion; use sonth and gluten-free hing (Jain rule: no onion, garlic or root vegetables)

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so halal-safe; fried, salty (about 1,150 mg sodium) and sweet-sauced, so better as an iftar starter than for sehri

jain.reason: drop garlic, fresh ginger and spring onion (onion family); use dry ginger powder (sonth) and gluten-free hing; check that the ketchup and chilli sauce have no onion or garlic

vegan.reason: no dairy, ghee, honey, egg, meat or fish (check that the ketchup and sauces carry no honey or fish extract)

sattvik.reason: skip garlic and the spring onion whites; use the greens only if onion-family greens are accepted, else coriander leaves

glutenFree.reason: maida (refined wheat flour) in the batter and ordinary soy sauce (brewed with wheat); the Gluten-free variant swaps in rice flour and gluten-free tamari

dairyFree.reason: no milk, curd, paneer, butter or ghee
